title: Auserene vs Rosebud: which AI journal fits you?

description: Auserene vs Rosebud compared from Rosebud's own pages, November 2026: memory, mood tracking, voice journaling, meditation, free plan, price, Android and privacy.
dek: Both AI journals talk back and remember. One leans on guided journals and weekly reports, the other on an evening conversation and a meditation made from your day.
titleOptions: Auserene vs Rosebud: which AI journal fits you?
Rosebud vs Auserene: AI journals compared on memory, meditation and price
Auserene or Rosebud? An honest comparison from one of them
Is Rosebud worth it? How it compares with Auserene

faq.a: It depends on what you want. Rosebud is stronger on guided, therapy-informed journals, weekly reports and platforms, since it runs on Android and the web. Auserene is stronger if you want a meditation made from your day, a memory you can read and edit, and a free plan. Auserene is iPhone only.

Not anymore. Rosebud's help center says it retired its free plan on September 30, 2026, though its homepage still said it was free to use in November 2026. Rosebud Bloom costs $12.99 a month or $107.99 a year in the US.

Yes, for Bloom subscribers. Rosebud's long-term memory recalls people, topics and how they relate, and Rosebud says it does better with topics than specific dates. It doesn't state whether you can view or edit individual memories.

Rosebud doesn't list a meditation or breathing feature on its site, App Store listing or help center. Auserene writes a guided meditation from each day's conversation and has eight guided meditation journeys.

faq.q: What is a good Rosebud alternative for iPhone?
faq.a: Auserene, if you want an evening conversation, editable memory and a meditation from your day. Day One with its Gold plan, if you want a long-term archive with AI added. Apple Journal, if you want something free and end-to-end encrypted with no AI chat.

informationGain: A disclosed head-to-head built only from Rosebud's own pages on November 19, 2026, including its free-plan retirement against a homepage that still says it's free, its admitted weakness with dates in long-term memory, its unpublished weekly usage limits and Thrive tiers, and the absence of any meditation feature, set against Auserene's readable memory and meditation made from your day.
